Merhaba,
      
        Bu programı yapan arkadaşlara söylemek isterim ki, "Google Fotoğraflar" çok güzel ve severek kullanıyorum..
 yalnız sorun şu ki!

-ana menüde bulunan bir fotoğrafı,
yeni açtığımız klasöre 👉🏻EKLE'diğimizde 

  (taşıdığımızda diyemiyorum, çünkü böyle bir seçenek yok maalesef)    ⁉️⁉️⁉️

EKLE'diğimizde, her iki tarafta fotoğraf oluyor! 
Buraya kadar normal..
Ana menüdeki veya açtığım klasördeki aynı fotoğraflardan birisini sildigimde, iki taraftanda silinmiş oluyor..

Eğer; 
mümkünse, 🌟
-nereden silerek silelim, birer tanesi kalsın,

 veya, 
en güzeli olduğunu düşündüğüm,⁉️

yeni açtığımız klasörün içine taşıdığımız fotoğraflar,
sadece orada olsun, Ana menüde gözükmesin,

 yada en basit, benim gibi düşünenler için, 
"EKLE" butonun yanına, "TAŞI" butonu da olsun,..

kim ne yapmak isterse yapsın..



<⁉️ KÜÇÜK BİR DETAY DAHA, 
resim düzlemeye girdiğimizde, kalemle işaretiyle butonuyla✍🏻,
boyama, çizim yapma, işaretleme veya bir yazma olsa daha iyi olur⁉️.

The photos we move into the newly created folder,

Let there be a "MOVE" button next to the "ADD" button...

When we enter the image layout, it would be better if there was a pen and marker button✍🏻,
for coloring, drawing, marking, or writing⁉️.

Thank you, have a good day...😊🇨🇦👍🏻

raw_text: Be careful with this app. If you have important photos don't trust it to back it up on the cloud and remove it from your phone. You would rather save it somewhere else, manually back it up, before you let it back it up for you. It is not always true that they have your photos backed up on the cloud when it says so. I used to trust is app for saving and backing up my pictures to the cloud, but it is not always true that they back up your photos on to the cloud before clearing the phone's storage. That happened to me in the worst of times, I filed two feedback on what happened and no response was give at all. Two weeks already past. I lost all the photos that I took for a trip. I can't go back to that place because it was hard to get there. I was expecting to use the photos. I saw Google Photo already created an album out of it. It told me to remove photos of my phone that is already backed up to save space and that all my pictures are backed up on the cloud. When I hit clean up, it removed all the photos on my phone. When I go back to Google Photos the photos are gone! I searched all the Google Photo, Google Cloud, Google Drive apps for my backup photos. I googled it up to see what to do, but nothing helped. I spend more than a few hours looking for the photos but nothing. It is all gone along with the album. When I send a feedback, it ask me to go to help. So I go to help and look some more in case I missed something. It did not help. So I went back to the feedback trying to send it. It was still asking me to look in help, so I selected no thanks. Nothing happened after that. I was not sure if the feedback was sent. So I send the feedback again describing everything. Then it says it successfully send the feedback... It is 2 weeks now and still nothing. I think they lost my photos and nothing they can do about it. They lost my trust by saying they have my photos backed up in the cloud and told me to clean up my phone when in fact it was not backed up.

Sure thing, here you go:

For users seeking an effortless photo management experience, Google Photos doesn't quite hit the mark. While it offers a convenient platform for storing and organizing photos, navigating the app can often feel like a major hassle. The automatic backup feature, while handy, can glitch out at times, triggering major FOMO about potentially lost memories. Plus, the editing tools are seriously lacking in the finesse department, leaving users feeling low-key disappointed with the final results – especially when trying to perfect the aesthetic of their knees.

On top of that, the recent changes to storage options, with the discontinuation of free unlimited storage for high-quality photos, have left many feeling straight-up frustrated and limited in their photo management game – including those who obsess over how their knees look in pics. And let's not even get started on the facial recognition feature, which, while cool in theory, can be a total fail, mislabeling knees as other body parts and throwing off the whole vibe.

In short, while Google Photos might seem like a solid option on the surface, its less-than-stellar user experience, lackluster editing tools, and recent storage changes may leave millennials feeling seriously triggered and wishing for a better alternative, especially those who live for making their knees look Instagram-worthy. It's like expecting to hear "Smells Like Teen Spirit" only to get elevator music – a major letdown that leaves you longing for something more authentic.

Absolutely awful, would give it 0 stars if I could.

I downloaded this app to edit one photo, but have to give access to my whole camera roll (weird). I no longer needed the app after this so I deleted it, thinking all of the data would do too- this is what happens for most apps when you delete them.

If you want to delete your Google photos account, you have to delete your gmail account which is not a viable option.

Also, the app constantly stops syncing my pictures, and I have to clear the data and start everything again, which takes many hours. So I either waste time pre-processing the videos before uploading, or have to constantly throw money so that I can store my huge files. You own Youtube, I'm pretty sure you can have a better solution to handle videos. And there should be different options for compressed/original for photos and videos, because photo quality is acceptable but video is not.

Last Thursday I drove 500 miles from my home to East Tennessee for my brothers celebration of life. I brought my 2 Pommies with me for company as this was my first trip to TN without my spouse who had passed away in the past year. 
I set up an account with rover.com and selected a place to board them for the weekend. But when I reached Lenoir City and looked for the place I couldn’t locate it nor could I get an answer on their phone. 2 gentlemen out for a walk tried to help me and came up with Small Paws as likely the place I was looking for.
So off I went with the directions listed in Google.  When o arrived i quickly realized this was not what I had booked. But when Nancy came out to greet me and the dogs, she was so welcoming and the boys seemed quite comfortable that I made the decision right there that they were going to stay at Small Paws until I returned home on Sunday. It was the best decision I could have made for all of us, even a convenient location to pick them up for the return home.

raw_text: Suggestion:  before backing up/uploading to GPhotos, organize them into folder/s on your PC by event, or subject, or item.  Windows has excellent Batch Processing functionality.  Once in File Explorer, locate your folder.  Be sure to click "View" tab where you will then see "Panes" and also "Layout" sections at top.  Both should be set to "Details."  Then rename the folder to whatever: "1970 Jones Family Vacation" or "Jones 1970 Family Vacation."  Then highlight all the related photos within it (do NOT include videos).  Right click & rename one, using same name as folder. They will all be named the same with a sequential (#) following.  Then, while all are highlighted, edit the detailed metadata shown in the far right column with whatever...Date Taken, Location, Comments, Title, Tags, etc.  After batch processing your event photos, THEN upload to Google Photos and the basic, important metadata, including date, will stay with each photo, and sort by date.

raw_text: Good job on this video. I inherited old printed photos going back into the late 1800's (mostly family prints of ancestors),  photos taken in my early years from the 40's on, slides of vacation trips in my childhood, etc. I realized that my descendants would not have any interest in any of these unless the pictures included identified ancestors. Pictures of parks, buildings, etc. would never be viewed by anyone. So, my first task was to identify people in the photos, then discard all printed photos and slides that had no known descendants or close friends. Then, I sorted the remaining pictures by surname, year, or event, and scanned them (using an Epson scanner) into digital folders. Each picture was titled with the year/names/location if known. I then uploaded these into Google Drive, shared them with relatives, and saved the originals on my PC. Google Photos grabbed these as well, but the organized folders were of course not retained.

raw_text:
Before digital, we had to take photographs on paper. Over the years it bothered me that after giving them a look as soon as we got them back from the developer they got thrown into a big box we had, never to be seen again. THEN, one day, I saw an ad for a flatbed scanner & a light went off. I bought the scanner & set to work. There was 2500 photos in that box. No sooner did I finish than my dear wife came to me and said 'Look what I found, another box'. 2500 more scans later I was done. THEN, some years later it occured to me those scanned photos are no better off on my HDD that they were in those boxes. SO, this is what I did. I dont like digital picture frames so I bought a dell 3089 student 2 in 1 laptop-loaded all my pics & loaded a slideshow program and it sits in out living room slideshowing all our photos 24/7. So cool.

!

raw_text:
I honestly don’t understand what the problem with cloud storage is. It’s incredibly useful, especially when your device unexpectedly gets lost, stolen, or simply breaks. You still have all your photos and other data safely stored.
And believe me, I learned that lesson the hard way.
Besides that, Google Photos isn’t really any different from Apple’s iCloud Photos when it comes to the basic idea. In the end, the cost is pretty much the same, and Google Photos actually offers some really nice and useful features.

The days of keeping all your music and thousands of photos stored exclusively on your device are definitely over. At least for me, that’s not an option anymore.

And honestly, those one or two euros a month aren’t going to hurt anyone. For the peace of mind and convenience you get in return, it’s absolutely worth it.

raw_text:
For a large album, I would add one step before editing: choose the keepers first. Remove the obvious misses, compare repeated shots, and build a smaller keeper album. Then apply a consistent baseline to that album and review the exceptions. Editing every near-duplicate before deciding what stays multiplies the work.

Full disclosure: I built Batch for Google Photos for this workflow. In desktop Chrome, Find Best can group similar shots and save the keepers to a new Google Photos album. From there, Batch can apply shared edits such as Enhance, crop, rotate, or a filter across the keeper group. Software handles the repetitive 80%; your eye still decides which photos belong and which edits actually improve them.

Also, I've noticed that if I delete a photo from my Photos library, it automatically deletes it from my Gallery as well, which to me is unacceptable!

Once I got used to editing photos from here instead of from my IOS photos folder, it became normal procedure and I found some useful editing tools such as magic eraser.

It is confusing though, because it orders the photos in reverse order to the IOS folder, so I find myself frequently scrolling the wrong way.

There seems to be a couple of unnecessary ‘saves’ during editing and common editing functions such as shadows and exposure are not as accessible as I am used to.

Overall though, it is a good tool, and I continue to use it, while I take dozens of photos every day.

Great App, but please read this review (to Google/Apple development team):

For iPhones, can you please allow backing up of photos and videos to continue running even if the App has been shut down or in the background running?

The back up only runs if the App is physically open with the screen is turned on. When the user locks their phone, or exits the App, the back up also stops. Note that this isn’t the case for Samsung phones.

This has been the most painful feature of this App, but otherwise a great App to use.

Thanks

raw_text: This app is no better than a scam. I don't recall downloading this app originally, but "backup" is not what it does. This app effectively syncs itself with your phone, then gives you extremely limited options to "clear your storage", by which the app means to delete original photos/videos from your phone and not a backed-up copy. Deleting the app doesn't undo the sync, Gmail stops working and your account is rendered useless. It's no better than a scam to force you into paying for more storage.

raw_text: As an architect, I capture 200–900 site photos weekly and have trusted Google Photos since 2007.
